findings.claim: The trigger 'or a failed record exists' never stops firing, because gauntlet/failed/<slug>.txt is written once and never removed (gauntlet-design.md:401). It also adds nothing, since `fail` itself already sets the files aside at fail time.
findings.failure_scenario: Run 1 is ruled defective and `fail` sets everything aside. Run 2 on the same slug (file route, gauntlet-intake-design.md:180, or standalone plan review under D-21) hears and approves a sound plan, then dies in spec review or the owner leaves at landing. Every later fresh run finds failed/<slug>.txt, sets the sound approved plan and spec aside again and re-hears from round 1. The rule 'unchanged task hears nothing' (plan-review-design.md:416) never holds for that slug again, and every run pays the Opus sessions again (CLAUDE.md 1.3).

findings.claim: The ruling moves both folders' round, review, ruling and cite files into one flat gauntlet/failed/<slug>.approved/ and names no layout or numbering for them. Plan and spec files share names, and a second set-aside on the same slug lands on the names the first one left there.
findings.failure_scenario: gauntlet/plans/<slug>.1.txt and gauntlet/specs/<slug>.1.txt, and likewise the .review.1.txt and .ruling.1.txt files, collide in one set-aside. Then the task is edited twice, or a hash-change set-aside is followed by a `fail` (D-39 numbers only verdict.<n>.txt). The move either overwrites the earlier evidence, or as `mv -n` exits non-zero. A non-zero exit fails the block's first node, so the run fails and every resume fails on a non-issue.

findings.claim: The ruling's list of files to set aside (round, review, ruling, cite) leaves out `<slug>-summary.N.md`, the reporter's write-once file in both plans/ and specs/. So a rerun that 'starts at round 1' still finds the old hearing's summaries.
findings.failure_scenario: After a set-aside, the new round 1 is APPROVED. gauntlet/plans/<slug>-summary.1.md from the old, defective hearing still exists. The reporter either refuses to write it again (written once) or the old file is never replaced. `docket` then shows the owner the old summary as the attention text, and `enter` copies it to approved/<slug>-summary.md (plan-review-design.md:399-400), which writing reads.

findings.claim: The 'recorded task hash differs' trigger can only read approved/<slug>.task.sha256, which `enter` writes only after approval. A task that changes while a hearing is unfinished is never detected, so a changed-task rerun does not start at round 1.
findings.failure_scenario: Run 1 approves the plan, has spec rounds 1-3 in progress, then dies. The owner edits the task and reruns. Plan review sees the hash differs and re-hears, producing a new plan. Spec review has no recorded spec hash and no failed record, so nothing is set aside, and the ledger continues spec round 4 on rounds written for the old plan. Its `enter` then records the new task's hash, hiding the mismatch for good. The same gap applies to a plan hearing interrupted before approval.

findings.claim: The ruling makes the plan-review and spec-review blocks read gauntlet/failed/<slug>.txt and write gauntlet/failed/<slug>.approved/. Neither design line is amended, so this breaks three of them: `fail` as 'the only writer of the checkout's gauntlet/failed/' (gauntlet-design.md:114, contracts.md H24), 'Only Clerk reads gauntlet/failed/' (:363), and the Homes row that forbids 'any other phase or role reading it' (:401).
findings.failure_scenario: Two failures follow. First, a builder following contracts.md H24 and Homes :401 builds the phase's first node without the failed-record check, so the ruling is undelivered; built with the check, the design breaks its own rule. Second, a hash-change set-aside creates gauntlet/failed/<slug>.approved/ for a slug that never failed. `ground` lists it (gauntlet-design.md:354-355), and Clerk's rule at :359-360 treats the slug as failed: it tries to read a gauntlet/failed/<slug>.txt that does not exist and forces a new slug.
